purpose: Test whether a fixed early-FPN foreground/background contrast improves Lean's existing multiscale memory-token ranking without changing detection, prompt, memory budget or model weights.
selection: Retrospective user-requested difficult cases; prior labels and outcomes were inspected. Sequence 3 is an engineering replay only. This is not an independent cohort.
mechanism: Keep the existing YOLO box, early-feature point prompt, 0.5 pooled-memory multiscale anchor, indexed RoPE and Lean 25% top-k. Compute normalized foreground and background descriptors using the first automatic prompt mask and existing reference_prototypes routine. For each new frame compute its FPN0 cosine difference, divide by 2 to match the anchor cosine range, area-average onto the memory grid, and blend with the existing pooled anchor score using a fixed 0.5 coefficient. Only the cached score consumed by the author's existing top-k changes; the previously queued TARR routing affinity remains unchanged. No additional detector call, re-detection, threshold or adaptive gate. Labels never enter inference.
controls: A strength-zero wrapper must reproduce the indexed reference masks, selections, positions and memory events exactly. Two independent label-free seq3 strength-zero replays and two independent strength-0.5 replays must match within condition, preserve model weights, show positive score changes, respect the same token budget and produce distinct masks and selected tokens before any candidate video scoring. Verify hooks are restored and the original TARR queue is unchanged. All scored runs use the same fixed coefficient; no sequence-dependent selection.
scoring: Run the four videos with the same first detector box and indexed baseline. Independently rescore every saved candidate and reference mask on all labeled frames and matched historical frame IDs. Report sequence Dice, false alarms and prompt initialization. No use of labels before each video finishes or at inference.
limitations: The initial reference is label-empty on seq20 and seq23. Prior read-only AUC evidence is mixed and does not establish token utility. Feature similarity need not mean causal segmentation benefit. Four selected sequences cannot support generalization; no per-sequence oracle switching.
